site.name: migration-atlas
site.summary: Migration Atlas — animal migration tracking (local demo) Fictional global animal-tracking atlas. Local fixture for UXBench. Open `index.html` directly. Page `index.html` — Atlas Three columns: left filter rail, center map + player, right inspector. The map is a hand-rolled SVG world (equirectangular projection) drawn from inline continent polygons and lon/lat graticules. Seven species are pre-loaded, each with a per-individual synthetic track of 12 monthly waypoints. Filters (left): species toggles with sample size counts, study year, display toggles (trail line, monthly position dots, stop-over polygons). Player (below map): slider scrubs through January → December. Play / pause button animates the season; speed selector controls cadence. As the slider advances, individuals' trails extend.

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full migration-atlas system, prioritizing the primary data visualization flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The atlas is generally functional and stable on both desktop and mobile, with filters, playback, and map updates responding without crashes or clipping. The biggest usability issues are mobile touch friction and weak state feedback: several controls are far too small to tap comfortably, and the study-year selector can change without the visible heading/summary making the change feel reliable. A few untested navigation links remain, but coverage is near-complete for the main data-viz flow.

exploration_plan.goal: Critically explore the primary map-based migration tracking flow in Migration Atlas, verify filter/player/inspector interactions across study years and species combinations, and check adjacent navigation and mobile usability for the most important controls.
exploration_plan.summary: Start with the main visualization on index.html and validate the intended end-to-end flow: species filtering, study-year switching, month scrubbing, play/pause, speed changes, and inspection by clicking trails/dots/tags. Then probe adjacent top-nav and view actions, and use a few representative species/state combinations to see how the map, summary metrics, and inspector update together. Finish with a mobile viewport pass focused on the same critical controls, especially those already flagged as small tap targets.
assumptions: The site is effectively a single-page local demo with all known functionality on index.html.
Top navigation items other than Explore may be placeholders or in-page links, so their value should be validated primarily for safe behavior and no broken states.
The map interactions are expected to work on inline SVG elements representing trails, monthly positions, and individual tags.
The 2026 season is in progress and may have different completeness or behavior from 2024/2025.
risk_hotspots: Species checkbox list in the left rail: very small tap targets on mobile and likely the main source of filter-state complexity.
Study year selector: switching among 2024, 2025, and 2026 may change available individuals, counts, and map state.
Month slider and Play button: core temporal controls that can desync map state if playback/scrubbing is buggy.
Speed selector: potential cadence issues during animation.
Map trail/dot/tag click targets: likely tricky SVG hit areas and the main path to the inspector panel.
Show trail / Show monthly positions / Show stop-over polygons toggles: important rendering switches that could expose layering or state bugs.
Cite this view and Save view buttons: high-value actions that should not fail silently if implemented.
Navigation links Explore, Studies, Submit a track, Methods, About: likely placeholder or partial flows that should be checked for safe transitions and recovery.

phases.title: Baseline map and control sanity
phases.objective: Confirm the default 2025 season state loads correctly and that the core controls are present and responsive before deeper interaction.
key_checks: Verify default species selection, current month, active individual count, and aggregate stats match the loaded state.
Confirm month slider, play/pause, and speed selector are all usable from the initial view.
Check that the right inspector panel shows guidance text when no individual is selected.
Inspect whether visible map layers correspond to the default display toggles (trail and monthly positions on, stop-over polygons off).
exit_criteria: Default view understood and no blocking UI or rendering failures observed.
At least one successful state change is demonstrated from the baseline without errors.

phases.title: Filter and season matrix
phases.objective: Exercise the left-rail filters to validate species toggles, species search, and study-year switching with attention to count and map-state changes.
key_checks: Use the species search box to narrow the list, then clear it and verify labels/counts remain consistent.
Toggle several species on and off, including the low-count species and the swarm aggregate, and observe changes in species shown and individual totals.
Switch between 2024, 2025, and 2026 seasons and verify the map and summary metrics update appropriately.
Check whether selected species persist or reset across season changes in a sensible way.
exit_criteria: All visible species controls have been exercised at least once, including search and season switching.
Observed no broken selections, impossible counts, or stale labels after state changes.

phases.title: Temporal playback and rendering toggles
phases.objective: Validate the month-based migration animation and the display-layer toggles that alter how the data is rendered.
key_checks: Scrub the month slider across early, middle, and late-year positions to ensure the title, current month, trails, and active individual behavior update.
Use Play/Pause to animate through months and confirm the slider advances and can be stopped cleanly.
Change speed among available settings and verify cadence changes during playback.
Toggle Show trail, Show monthly positions, and Show stop-over polygons individually and in combinations to confirm layer visibility changes without breaking the map.
exit_criteria: Month progression is seen to affect the map and summary state.
All three display toggles and the speed selector have been tested in at least one meaningful combination.

phases.title: Individual inspection and map hit-target validation
phases.objective: Confirm that clicking map objects opens or updates the individual inspector and that the key species/trail elements are distinguishable and interactive.
key_checks: Click representative trails, dots, and tags for at least two species and confirm the inspector panel updates from the generic prompt to a specific individual.
Check that the selected individual affects aggregate stats or displayed context in a coherent way.
Verify the interaction remains usable after filter changes and different month positions.
Look for any mismatch between clicked visible geometry and the inspector content, especially on dense or overlapping tracks.
exit_criteria: At least two distinct inspection interactions succeed from the map.
Inspector updates are consistent with the clicked species/track and no dead hit areas are observed in the sampled cases.

phases.title: Adjacent actions and recovery paths
phases.objective: Probe the non-core actions and nearby navigation for safe behavior, expected affordances, and recovery from any transient state.
key_checks: Activate Cite this view and Save view to verify whether they open a dialog, copy action, or other visible confirmation.
Open top navigation links Explore, Studies, Submit a track, Methods, and About to determine whether they are inert placeholders, in-page anchors, or route to valid content.
If any action changes the page state, confirm there is a way back to the main atlas view without losing browser stability.
Check that no console/network errors appear after these actions.
exit_criteria: Adjacent controls have been sampled and their behavior characterized.
Any non-core flow either works safely or is confirmed as placeholder behavior without breakage.

phases.title: Mobile viewport regression pass
phases.objective: Repeat the most important interactions on mobile viewport to assess tapability, layout stability, and control usability under constrained space.
key_checks: Verify the main layout remains usable and the map, filters, and inspector are still accessible on mobile.
Repeat one species toggle, one season switch, one month scrub, one play/pause action, and one map inspection on mobile.
Specifically check the small tap targets already flagged in prescan, including nav links and species checkboxes, for mis-taps or difficult activation.
Confirm the speed selector and month slider remain operable without overlap or clipping.
exit_criteria: Critical interactions succeed on mobile or are clearly identified as problematic due to tap-target size.
At minimum, the core filter-player-inspector loop has been verified in mobile viewport.

coverage_targets.pages: visit all known HTML pages; in this site, that means thoroughly exercising the single known page index.html
coverage_targets.features: exercise the filter rail, season selector, display toggles, month slider, play/pause, speed selector, map inspection, and view/action buttons
coverage_targets.mobile: repeat the core filter, timeline, playback, and inspection checks in mobile viewport, with special attention to the flagged small tap targets

notes: Because the prescan shows only one HTML file, emphasis should be on state-space coverage rather than page navigation breadth.
Prioritize representative species rather than every possible combination, but include at least one high-count and one low-count species plus the swarm aggregate.
Treat 2026 as a likely edge case because it is marked in progress.

findings.user_goal: Filter species quickly on a phone without mis-taps
findings.problem: The species filter checkboxes are extremely small touch targets, making reliable selection on mobile difficult even though the filters work when tapped successfully.
findings.evidence: On mobile, each species checkbox is 13×13px; the layout warnings flag multiple species inputs as below the 44px mobile guidance, and the trajectory notes repeatedly call them 'very small touch targets.'
findings.why_it_matters: Users trying to refine the atlas on a phone will likely struggle to hit the intended species, leading to frustration and accidental toggles.
findings.suggestion: Increase the tap area for each species row, not just the checkbox square—make the full label row clickable and add more vertical spacing.

findings.user_goal: Use playback controls comfortably on mobile
findings.problem: The primary playback controls are also below mobile touch guidance, especially the Play button and speed selector, which makes season scrubbing and animation control feel cramped.
findings.evidence: The Play button is only 22×40px, the speed select is 71×36px, and the layout warnings flag the Play control as below the 44px guidance.
findings.why_it_matters: If users cannot easily pause, resume, or adjust speed, they lose control over the animation and may miss important map changes.
findings.suggestion: Enlarge the play button to a square 44px minimum target and provide a larger, more prominent speed control with clearer spacing.

findings.user_goal: Change the study year and understand that the atlas has switched seasons
findings.problem: The study-year dropdown can be changed, but the visible heading/summary can remain on a different season label, creating a state/label mismatch.
findings.evidence: In mobile testing, selecting the study-year control changed the dropdown to '2024 season,' but the main heading still read 'Migration Atlas — 2025 season'; earlier notes also describe the season selector landing on the wrong option or not visibly applying.
findings.why_it_matters: A mismatch between the control value and the page heading undermines trust in the data state and makes users unsure which season they are viewing.
findings.suggestion: After season changes, update the title/summary immediately and add a short inline confirmation so the selected season is unmistakable.

findings.user_goal: Understand and use the season selector with assistive or low-vision interaction
findings.problem: The study-year select has no visible label, aria-label, or placeholder in the DOM summary, reducing its clarity as a form control.
findings.evidence: The browser observation explicitly reports a missing input label for the select, and the DOM summary shows the select name as the raw options text with an empty label/placeholder.
findings.why_it_matters: Users relying on screen readers or scanning forms quickly may not understand what the dropdown controls, especially when it is separated from the season heading.
findings.suggestion: Add a visible label tied to the select and an accessible name that clearly states it controls the study year/season.

findings.user_goal: Know whether a filter action changed the atlas state
findings.problem: Some interactions update the page quietly, but the feedback is inconsistent; for example, filter and season changes sometimes only show a subtle dropdown value change or a count change without a clear confirmation message.
findings.evidence: The trajectory notes say the speed selector changed with 'no visible in-UI status text' beyond the dropdown, and the season selector sometimes changed without an obvious visible-text update; the user has to infer success from scattered counts/headings.
findings.why_it_matters: When the atlas is dense and animated, subtle state changes are easy to miss, so users may repeat actions or doubt whether a control worked.
findings.suggestion: Add brief inline status feedback near the player or inspector when season, speed, or filter states change.

findings.user_goal: Reach other sections like Explore, Methods, or Submit a track
findings.problem: The top navigation items were not fully exercised, and the ones tested behave like placeholder anchors rather than clearly distinct destinations.
findings.evidence: The session memory shows 'Explore,' 'Methods,' and 'Submit a track' remain unvisited, while clicking 'Studies' and 'About' only appended a hash (`index.html#`) and kept the atlas in place.
findings.why_it_matters: If users expect deeper content or distinct pages, placeholder-style links can feel broken or unfinished.
findings.suggestion: Either make these links clearly in-page sections or label them as internal jumps/coming-soon items so expectations are set correctly.

findings.user_goal: Interact with the map to inspect an individual on mobile
findings.problem: The attempted mobile map click failed due to a null target, so this flow still lacks direct evidence that a user can reliably tap map objects to inspect an individual.
findings.evidence: The final mobile step failed with 'Click failed for null' and no inspector change; the observations note that the map click did not select an item and the inspector stayed on the default guidance state.
findings.why_it_matters: Map inspection is a core task in a data visualization atlas; if hit areas or targetability are unclear, users cannot complete the main exploratory workflow.
findings.suggestion: Make map objects more obviously tappable on mobile and provide larger hit regions or a dedicated selection affordance.

findings.user_goal: Use the small filter rail without visual crowding
findings.problem: The filter rail is readable but tightly packed on mobile, with several controls stacked close together, which can make the panel feel cramped even when it does not clip.
findings.evidence: Multiple notes say the mobile layout remains intact but the left rail has tightly packed controls; the screenshot shows many 13px checkboxes, a long select, and dense label rows in a narrow column.
findings.why_it_matters: Dense control clusters increase tap errors and make scanning the current filter state slower.
findings.suggestion: Increase row height and spacing in the filter rail, and consider grouping related controls or collapsing secondary options on small screens.

gaps: 3 browser action(s) failed and should be retried or analyzed.
